messages.subject: expected AC density surface = predictDsurface()? -- Durbach et al., 2024, Biometrics
parts:
Hi all, 
I just read Durbach et al. 2024 in Biometrics (10.1093/biomtc/ujad020). They caution against using predicted AC surfaces as density surfaces. Am I wrong to feel that really, there's "nothing new here", since Murray has had that section "this is not a density surface" in the secr documentation for a long time? At least I think that's what Durbach et al. seem to argue, right? Or do I miss something big? 

I'm still a bit unsure of what they're talking about, because of the differing terminology between authors and because I just came back from a very distracting vacation: 

If I have a SECR model with inhomogeneous density (several spatial density covariates) and use predictDsurface() to create a map -- does that correspond to what Durbach et al. describe in section 2.1.: Expected AC density surface. 

"The first we call the “expected AC density” surface. This is D(s|β), the intensity function of the underlying point process that is assumed to have generated the ACs. We use the term “expected,” because the intensity of the point process at s is approximately the expected number of ACs per unit area generated by the process in some small region surrounding s (and is exactly the expectation as the area of the region approaches 0). This quantity depends only on the parameters of the point process, and is not specific to any particular realization of points. (...)" .

I could really use some elucidation here. Thank you all. 

Mirjam Barrueto, 
PhD student, UCalgary

messages.subject: Re: expected AC density surface = predictDsurface()? -- Durbach et al., 2024, Biometrics
parts:
Hi Mirjam,

Not adding anything Murray hasn't said, but as a co-author of that paper I thought I should say something! You're totally right - predictDsurface gives you expected AC density surfaces. It's the other surface (what we called predicted AC location surfaces / what you get from fx.total) that are often misinterpreted, though not by secr users, maybe because of the warning in the vignette.

You're also right about it not being new. We do quote the vignette, and a similar warning in the Royle et al SCR book, but since misinterpretations still happen we tried to flesh these out.

Ian

parts:
Thank you very much for this comment and confirmation, Ian! These technical papers often come a bit as a shock to me, because the language between researchers, groups, Bayesian vs not, differ and it’s not always clear to me right away which concepts are actually the same. And which are new issues that I had not considered yet but should! I read your paper just as I was creating several expected AC density surfaces for a manuscript 😉.

...side note, a collaborator has been plotting multi-year time series of predicted AC location surfaces of a declining wildlife population to get a sense for where changes in our study area may be the biggest. Our thought is that if the environmental variables stay roughly the same across time in most of the study area (which we know very well), but individual distribution changes, the places where the changes are the largest may say something about underlying causes. This wouldn't necessarily be reflected in expected AC density surfaces because our data isn't high res enough to model such (localized) changes. So, I do feel that there may be valuable information contained in those predicted AC location surfaces about certain processes, just as you suggest in the paper.

Cheers,

Mirjam
